headline: Approved Superintendent's 2025-2026 evaluation as Proficient; approved $101,647.57 in prior year payments; referred Nelson Place School petitions to administration.
summary: The meeting went into executive session to discuss collective bargaining with the Educational Association of Worcester, then reconvened in open session. Consent agenda items, including donations, were approved, and a Carnegie Hall digital curriculum donation was approved in a separate vote. Four public petitions by Joey Ford were referred to the administration, and the Superintendent's evaluation was approved and filed.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, except the Carnegie Hall Musical Explorers digital curriculum donation, 9-0.
Approved the Carnegie Hall Musical Explorers Digital curriculum donation, 9-0.
Referred c&p 6-10 (Ford), concerning a Nelson Place School report, to the Administration, 9-0.
Referred c&p 6-11 (Ford), concerning a public Nelson Place School report, to the Administration, 9-0.
Referred c&p 6-12 (Ford), concerning outside-counsel spending, to the Administration, 9-0.
Referred c&p 6-13 (Ford), concerning cybersecurity safeguards, to the Administration, 9-0.

Approved the Community-Based Out of School Social and Recreational Program grant of $43,384.50, the RALIE grant of $2,000, 27 prior year payments totaling $101,647.57, and a $20,000 prior year payment for a missed educational level, 9-0.
Approved and filed the 2025-2026 Superintendent summative evaluation, rated Proficient overall, 9-0.
Approved the 2027 School Committee meeting dates, except November 4, 2027, which will be reselected, 9-0.
Approved the Report of the Superintendent Schedule for the 2026-2027 school year, 9-0.
Rescheduled the November 5, 2026 meeting to November 12, 2026, 9-0.
Referred gb 6-92 (Biancheria), on MassHire services for students, to the Administration, 9-0.
Approved and filed the change to the IRS mileage reimbursement rate from $0.725/mile to $0.76/mile, 9-0.

 gb 6-88 (Petty) 
  (August 13, 2026) 
 Summative Evaluation 
 To conduct an evaluation of the Superintendent for the 2025-2026 school year. 
 
 Mayor Petty reviewed the evaluation review process. He reviewed the Committee 
assessment on the Superintendent’s Goals. District Goal #1, District Goal #2 and the 
Professional Practice goals were graded as “met” and District Goal #3 and the 
Student Learning Goal were graded as “significant progress.” 
 
 Mayor Petty went into more detail while describing each goal, focus indicators, and 
evidence provided to determine the evaluation criteria. He also provided select 
comments from School Committee members, which were provided in their 
evaluations.  
 
 The evaluation standards were graded as follows: 
 Standard I: Proficient 
 Standard II: Proficient 
 Standard III: Proficient 
 Standard IV: Proficient 
 Overall Summative Evaluation grade: Proficient 
  
 Member Mailman asked when individual evaluation documents will be posted to the 
WPS website. Mayor Petty noted that it would be done no later than Monday, August 
17, 2026.  
 
 Member Johnson spoke regarding the evaluation process. He also gave kudos to the 
Superintendent’s cabinet, teachers, paraprofessionals, and all WPS employees. 
Member Johnson also noted there is some room for improvement in family and 
community engagement and looks forward to working with Superintendent Allen in 
the coming year. He stated that while he does believe that there is room for 
improvement, WPS is still in a great place.
